cards.title: OpenStax Chemistry 2e — Molecular Structure and Polarity; Hybrid Atomic Orbitals
supports: Single, double, and triple bonds each count as one electron-domain / VSEPR electron-density region around a central atom.
Steric number = number of sigma bonds + number of lone pairs on the central atom.
Four electron domains correspond to tetrahedral electron-domain geometry (sp3 hybridisation).
Three electron domains correspond to trigonal planar electron-domain geometry (sp2 hybridisation).
Two electron domains correspond to linear electron-domain geometry (sp hybridisation).
Molecular shape describes positions of atomic nuclei only; non-bonding lone pairs cause molecular shape to deviate from electron-domain geometry.
The number of hybrid orbitals formed strictly equals the number of valence atomic orbitals combined (conservation of orbitals).
Hybridisation is a localized Valence Bond rationalization of observed geometry, not an independent experimental observable.

cards.title: OpenStax Chemistry: Atoms First 2e — Valence Bond Theory; Multiple Bonds
supports: Sigma (σ) bonds result from head-on (coaxial) overlap with electron density concentrated along the internuclear axis.

Pi (π) bonds result from lateral (side-on) overlap of parallel unhybridised p orbitals with electron density concentrated above and below the internuclear axis, containing a nodal plane in the internuclear plane.
A double bond consists of 1 σ bond + 1 π bond; a triple bond consists of 1 σ bond + 2 π bonds.

In linear sp centres with two double bonds (like CO2) or one triple bond (like HCN), the two π bonds are mutually perpendicular (orthogonal), utilizing distinct unhybridised 2p orbitals (e.g., 2py and 2pz).

cards.title: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry Part I — Unit 4: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure
supports: VSEPR rules governing bond angles and shapes for BF3 (trigonal planar), NH3 (trigonal pyramidal), H2O (bent), CH4 (tetrahedral), CO2 (linear).
Concept of hybridization: sp, sp2, sp3 mixing of atomic orbitals in carbon, boron, and nitrogen compounds.
Shapes and hybridisation of ethene (C2H4) and ethyne/HCN, detailing sigma backbone and unhybridised p-orbital lateral overlap.
Distinction between observable bond parameters (bond lengths, bond angles from diffraction/spectroscopy) and the theoretical model of directional hybrid orbitals.

advanced_extension_source_requirement: NOT_APPLICABLE: no amide, allene, radical or delocalisation claim is required for Q1–Q10 in this D2 brief. The set is fully grounded in standard introductory VSEPR, localized Valence Bond hybridisation, and sigma/pi decomposition.
